findings.title: The face-Day frame reverses its verdict
findings.claim: The faces in this ayah are placed in the already evoked Day-frame, and the final predicate gives that same face-centered scene its positive verdict.
findings.mechanism: The face word supplies the visible subjects and the deictic time word retrieves the earlier frame; the ease predicate makes the contrast arise within one event-time.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees this as the matched positive half of the face sorting, rather than an isolated statement about pleasant faces.
findings.containment: The frame comparison deepens the local statement that faces are at ease and does not turn the ayah into a claim about every other face scene.

epistemic.reason: Both cited word-analysis records are trusted and directly describe the repeated frame and reversed predicate.

findings.title: An open class of faces enters
findings.claim: The ayah opens with newly introduced, indefinite faces as the nominative subject whose condition will be stated.
findings.mechanism: The broken plural is nominative and indefinite, while the verbless predicate assigns one visible condition to that fresh class; the form introduces people through their countenances.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader meets a visible class rather than a named group, with the faces ready to receive the clause's verdict.
findings.containment: The carrier remains the concrete face noun; indefiniteness opens the class without supplying an identity beyond the ayah.

epistemic.reason: Accepted QAC alignment and trusted attachment evidence directly establish the subject and predicate relation.

findings.title: The open plural moves into the Day-marker
findings.claim: The indefinite face-class is heard moving directly into the Day-marker before the verdict arrives.
findings.mechanism: The plural's final nunation is immediately followed by the temporal compound, so the sound carries the newly opened subject into its event-time.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader hears the scene remain open for a beat before time fixes where the faces' state will be disclosed.
findings.containment: This is a form-and-sound effect attached to the local sequence; it does not add a separate lexical sense to the faces.

epistemic.reason: Trusted form and sound records directly state the indefinite ending and immediate temporal continuation.

findings.title: The faces remain exposed fronts
findings.claim: The concrete faces also press toward exposed front and publicly legible standing while remaining the faces named by the noun.
findings.mechanism: The face word can meet the predicate as an outward surface under encounter and standing, so the visible condition carries a local front-facing and status pressure.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader senses wellbeing displayed on an exposed human front, where condition can be encountered and read.
findings.containment: The packet supports this as a local qualifying pressure; the noun continues to mean concrete faces rather than directions or social rank alone.

epistemic.reason: The cited support explicitly narrows the orientation and status pressure under the concrete local noun.

findings.title: Countenance makes condition public
findings.claim: The face is the public surface on which the condition becomes readable, so the ayah presents wellbeing rather than hiding it as private feeling.
findings.mechanism: The concrete countenance is the carrier and the predicate places ease upon it; the person's disclosed state therefore meets the observer on the face.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the blessed condition made legible on the human surface that can be encountered.
findings.containment: The claim concerns public manifestation through the face and does not erase the ordinary bodily reference or infer an unseen inner state beyond the supplied contact.

epistemic.reason: Trusted face analysis and the accepted local face/front support directly ground the public-surface relation.

findings.title: A fresh human tableau begins

findings.mechanism: A new nominal subject begins the clause and no attachment carries the earlier food-chain syntax across the boundary, so the discourse turns from provision to visible persons.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader feels the scene change from failed sustenance to the faces on which ease will now be displayed.
findings.containment: The boundary sharpens the local subject and predicate without making the ayah depend on a wider sequence than the supplied local evidence.

epistemic.reason: Trusted clause-boundary and face-subject records directly support the new tableau.
